OrPen owns public notebook source because each notebook demonstrates a public
component or cross-section from this PDK. SCGSim owns every reusable simulation
stage: semantic geometry, mesh/config generation, handoff, result resolution,
and reports.

Notebook folders classify the simulated thing first. A thing may contain
Palace, AEDT, single-run, or sweep notebooks without duplicating runtime logic.

Start with the [Simulation requirements](../notebooks.qmd), then select an
example for the observation it can actually support:

- Pad examples: [capacitance](requirements/electrostatic-capacitance.qmd),
  [eigenmode](requirements/eigenmode.qmd), and [EPR / loss](requirements/epr-loss.qmd).
- CPW examples: [Driven Terminal](requirements/driven-terminal.qmd),
  [Driven Modal](requirements/driven-modal.qmd), [Q3D AC / RL](requirements/q3d-acrl.qmd),
  and [Q2D cross-sections](requirements/q2d-cross-section.qmd).
- Shared resonator examples: [Lumped RLC eigenmode](requirements/lumped-rlc-eigenmode.qmd)
  and [Lumped/Wave Terminal](requirements/driven-terminal.qmd), with their own
  explicitly authored loads and excitation; ordinary eigenmode is not a substitute.

Pages explain the intended physical product and tool behavior. Notebooks own
case settings, source observations and explicit operation stages. The current
suite is **SOURCE ONLY / CONVERGING**: authoring and clean publication artifacts
do not establish native geometry, mesh or solved-result coverage.

## Current source-only suite

The suite targets [SCGSim v2 RC1](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/scgsim/tree/85d8bedb733b1e17737d935029618351b30ea5de)
in a separate consumer environment. Follow each source's environment instructions;
the ordinary project environment and pins are unchanged. Canonical QMDs own
Markdown, code order and settings. Clean derived IPYNBs are downloadable
publication/execution artifacts, not another editable authority.

The three resonator QMDs share one authoring cell. Download its companion
<a href="../notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/_source_input.qmd" download>_source_input.qmd</a>
to the same directory when rebuilding those QMDs. Their derived IPYNBs already
contain that cell and do not need the companion.

The shared resonator cases use the selected reproducible 17-bridge source pair:
launcher/Lumped and boundary-cut/Wave geometry serve distinct excitation
questions. Geometry source observations, preparation, native readback, solve,
returned-run Resolve and Report remain separate stages. Resolve/Report do not
request another solve.

Current PDK base metal is 0.1 µm. The explicitly authored Q2D section instead
keeps its Nb 0.2 µm thickness, 10 µm gap and 40 µm grounds; it is not an
automatic slice or equivalent result of a 3D coupon. Concrete settings remain
in the notebooks rather than being repeated in requirement pages.

### Driven Modal compatibility blocker

The selected SCGSim checkpoint has no body-first Driven Modal interface.
The [historical Modal authoring note](../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_hfss_driven_modal.ipynb)
and its <a href="../notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_hfss_driven_modal.qmd" download>nonexecutable QMD</a>
retain the authored case without guessed native-object bindings. A usable
current Modal notebook remains incomplete; Terminal is not a substitute.

Historical output is not execution of these revised sources. The current suite
does not claim that every branch is complete, supported or natively observed.

#### RF-grounded electrostatic evidence

The current comparison uses one common public boundary: `xmon_pad` is the sole
terminal; four couplers, both die grounds, and eight bumps form one Ground;
the exterior has its natural zero-charge boundary. Lateral vacuum padding is
0 µm and the z padding is ±1000 µm. The public geometry is
309.5 µm × 24.65 µm with a 20 µm gap and silicon εr = 11.9.

| Model | Selected C11 (fF) | EC/h (MHz) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Palace A′ — substrate-face sheet | 99.3030125873 | 195.0618497866 |
| Palace A — metal-gap-equivalent sheet | 99.78426582503 | 194.1210787543 |
| Palace B — finite metal | 99.44860318002 | 194.7762834798 |
| AEDT Q3D — physical-geometry diagnostic | 97.52280968178212 | 198.6225518713 |

![Palace AMR traces and the four selected RF-grounded C11 values.](../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/Kosen2024_Xmon/evidence/comparison.png){fig-alt="Palace A-prime, A, and Route B AMR traces beside a bar chart comparing their selected grounded C11 values with the AEDT Q3D diagnostic."}

The Palace rows are the last complete hash-bound snapshots from receipts that
remain failed after exit 137; they are not completed-run claims. Q3D completed
20 adaptive passes, but its capacitance matrix stopped at 0.429585% rather
than the requested 0.1%; its AC-RL extraction converged. These differences are
evidence only: no solver-agreement Gate or scientific acceptance is claimed.

Exact identities, receipt hashes, and unrounded values remain in the
[run-set manifest](../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/Kosen2024_Xmon/evidence/run_set.json)
and [results table](../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/Kosen2024_Xmon/evidence/results.csv).
